title: ScVal Bool encoded as 2, outside the XDR boolean range
caps_note: A cross-cutting encoding rule rather than a CAP: it applies to every XDR value of every protocol
why: An XDR bool is 0 or 1 (RFC 4506 section 4.4). stellar-core's decoder reads 2 as TRUE, a decoder that tests for 1 reads it as false, and a strict one refuses it; whichever value is read re-encodes to different bytes than the input.

source.reason: XDR booleans are 0 or 1 (RFC 4506 section 4.4); stellar-core re-serialises canonically, so a boolean of 2 is never in core output

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 28.0.0, 28.0.1 and 30.0.0 under limits-default and limits-none: the value decodes as ScVal::Bool(false) and re-encodes as 0000000000000000, the opposite of stellar-core's reading. Reported upstream as rs-stellar-xdr#622.
known_divergences.evidence: probe vector 6a (evidence/sdk-matrix), executed on stellar-xdr 28.0.0, 28.0.1 and 30.0.0; xcc conform run --columns 'rust@*' --entries 'xdr-strict/bool-value-2'

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 17.0.0 and 17.0.1 (xdrlib3 0.1.1): xdr.SCVal.from_xdr_bytes decodes the value as True and re-encodes it as 0000000000000001, the same reading as stellar-core 30.0.0 (evidence/core-print-xdr/out/bool-2.txt). Status wont_fix: the SDK reads the value as the network does, so there is nothing to change; recorded so the cell is expected.
